channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: BoC expected to keep interest rate unchanged as prices stay elevated and growth slows
item.description: The Bank of Canada (BoC) is widely expected to keep its policy rate unchanged at 2.25% on Wednesday. This would be the fifth consecutive gathering with the bank keeping its hand steady.

item.title: Brent: Limited reaction to US–Iran strikes – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Hardman and Lockhart report that Brent Oil prices have shown a muted response to renewed US–Iran military exchanges, trading near recent lows after briefly dipping below USD 90 per barrel.

item.title: Canadian Dollar gains as US inflation data fails to boost the US Dollar, BoC decision eyed
item.description: The Canadian Dollar (CAD) strengthens against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday as traders digest the latest US Consumer Price Index (CPI) data and await the Bank of Canada's (BoC) interest rate decision.

item.title: Breaking: United States CPI inflation rises to three-year high at 4.2% in May
item.description: Annual inflation in the United States (US), as measured by the change in the Consumer Price Index (CPI), rose to its highest level in three years at 4.2% in May, from 3.8% in April. This reading came in line with the market expectation.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Range-bound outlook near 0.70–0.71 against US Dollar
item.description: Rabobank’s Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley highlights that the Australian Dollar (AUD) has fallen from a top G10 performer to the bottom of recent rankings as growth momentum fades and USD strength weighs.

item.title: Aluminium: Exports and speculative longs increase – ING
item.description: ING strategists Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey highlight that Chinese unwrought Aluminium and product exports rose strongly in May to the highest level since November 2024, helped by overseas demand after Middle East disruptions.

item.title: WTI Oil price bounces back to near $88 as Trump warns further military actions against Iran
item.description: The West Texas Intermediate (WTI), futures on NYMEX, turns flat slightly above $88.00 in the European trade on Wednesday after clawing back its early losses.

item.title: South African Rand: Growth quality weighs on ZAR – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Volkmar Baur notes that stronger-than-expected South African GDP growth masks weak underlying domestic demand, with consumption and private investment soft while government spending dominates.

item.title: Japanese Yen hits fresh lows at 160.50 US Dollar as BoJ’s Ueda is hospitalized
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) extends its decline on Wednesday, threading further beyond the key 160.00 per US Dollar (USD), which is considered a red zone for Tokyo intervention.

item.title: US President Trump says he is close to ordering new strikes against Iranian infrastructure
item.description: United States (US) President Donald Trump has stated in an interview with Fox News that he is close to ordering new military strikes against Iranian power plants and bridges, adding that Tehran is "taking too long to make a deal".

item.title: Gold extends sell-off ahead of US CPI inflation data
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) slides to fresh 11-week lows on Wednesday as mounting speculation that the Federal Reserve (Fed) could raise interest rates later this year weighs on demand for the non-yielding metal. At the time of writing, XAU/USD is trading around $4,163, down 2.30% on the day.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Flows reverse as BoC looms – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Bob Savage highlights a sharp reversal in Canadian Dollar (CAD) flows ahead of the June Bank of Canada (BoC) decision versus April, when CAD was generally bid.

item.title: US Dollar: Upside risks persist on sticky inflation – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes that the US Dollar retains upside risk as US inflation is expected to heat up in May and the disinflation trend has stalled.

item.title: Canada: Oil-driven inflation shifts BoC outlook – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Robert Both updates Canada’s macro outlook as higher Oil prices push WTI above $95 through Q4, lifting headline CPI to an average 2.9% over Q2/Q3.

item.title: $4,100: The immediate support for Gold
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) trades 2.1% lower at around $4,170 during the European trading session on Wednesday.

item.title: United States: Oil-driven price pressures and policy focus – UBS
item.description: UBS Chief Economist Paul Donovan expects May United States (US) headline consumer price inflation to rise as higher Oil-related costs are passed through to consumers. He notes firms can protect profit margins by raising prices while demand holds, with US consumers drawing on savings.

item.title: WTI Oil holds near seven-week lows sub-$87 despite US-Iran tensions
item.description: Crude prices are trading lower for the fifth consecutive day on Wednesday, with the US benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI) barrel trading at $86.60 at the time of writing, more than $4 down so far this week.

item.title: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda hospitalized: expected to miss June monetary policy
item.description: Bank of Japan (BoJ) Governor Kazuo Ueda has been hospitalized, according to a statement released by the central bank.

item.title: Bank of Canada: Policy hold risks highlighted – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Global Strategist Michael Every expects the Bank of Canada (BoC) to keep its policy rate at 2.25%, in line with Bloomberg consensus and market pricing.

item.title: US Dollar: AI-driven inflows support Dollar – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Volkmar Baur argues that a major US technology IPO could generate sizeable foreign capital inflows, supporting the US Dollar, particularly against the Euro.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Downside against US Dollar eyed as BoC holds – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s Elias Haddad highlights that USD/CAD has pulled back after testing a six‑month high but still risks grinding higher toward 1.4140.

item.title: Japanese Yen: CPI risks dominate against US Dollar – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman and Abdul-Ahad Lockhart note that recent US Dollar (USD) resilience and higher US yields have created a tougher backdrop for FX carry trades, while commodity-linked currencies lag.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) fell on Wednesday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $63.99 per troy ounce, down 2.11% from the $65.37 it cost on Tuesday.

item.title: Indian Rupee gains despite renewed Middle East conflicts, US CPI eyed
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) rises against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday after a flat opening. The USD/INR pair falls to near 95.15 even as Middle East tensions have flared up again, following the United States (US) retaliation against Iran over the shooting down of an American helicopter.

item.title: Experts agree: RBA’s next move will likely be an interest-rate cut, not a hike
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) underperforms its major currency pairs during the European trading session on Wednesday, trading 0.25% lower to near 0.7010 against the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Australian Dollar: 0.7000 support under pressure against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann report that AUD/USD spiked to 0.7071 before sliding to 0.7005 and closing at 0.7027. They see slightly stronger downside momentum but doubt a sustained break below 0.7000 in the very near term.

item.title: US Dollar: Core CPI focus keeps DXY supported – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner notes the Dollar is holding recent gains as markets await the US May CPI report, with expectations that firm core inflation will keep Federal Reserve hike pricing alive into December.

item.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: Could rebound toward six-month highs near 1.4000
item.description: USD/CAD loses ground for the second consecutive day, trading around 1.3930 during the European hours on Wednesday. However, the technical analysis of the daily chart indicates the pair is moving upwards within the ascending channel pattern, signaling an ongoing bullish bias.

item.title: Gold languishes near March low, below $4,200 as traders await US CPI report
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) maintains its heavily offered tone through the first half of the European session and currently trades near its lowest level since March 23, around the $4,180-$4,175 region.

item.title: Euro: Gains hinge on domestic demand – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu notes that recent EUR/USD support has come mainly from cross-border investors reducing hedges after the European Central Bank's (ECB) hawkish shift, bringing aggregate Euro holdings back to flat.
